title: Night-temperature variation added 3.5-5.2% to a fixed moth activity model in four British samples in 1993-2015
abstract: We tested how variation among sampling-night temperatures changes a fixed exponential moth activity model beyond mean temperature. We used 687 retained trap-months in England and Scotland in 1993-2003 and 2004-2015. With a fixed response of 14.4% per C, the median added activity multiplier was 3.5-5.2%. All four adjusted trend intervals included zero. Response scenarios, a stricter night-count rule and summer restriction also gave uncertain trends. The positive term follows from Jensen's inequality; its size and trend are empirical calibration results. The calculation gives an exact catch ratio only if baseline abundance and effort are constant across retained nights. It does not measure a population bias or identify a climate-change effect. Few sites, selected nights, inherited weather processing and the assumed response limit use. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and reproduction instructions are included. External record tables remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Added multiplier under a fixed exponential response, and four year-cluster trend intervals. The positive multiplier is a model consequence, not a measured population effect.
